helper.name: ensureUserExists
helper.signature: ensureUserExists({ id: String, name: String, email: String }) -> Promise<UserDocument>
helper.description: Guarantees a local User record exists for a person already resolved from the AD/directory typeahead, without a second server-side directory lookup (research.md R1/R2).
behavior: User.findById(id) first. If found, return it unchanged -- never overwrite name/email/roles on an existing record (FR-009).
If not found and email is missing or empty, throw a 400-shaped validation error -- never create a record with no deliverable address (FR-008).
If not found and email is present, create new User({ _id: id, name, email }) with roles: [] (the same shape the first-login flow in lib/auth/ldap.js already creates), save it, and return it.

added_field.name: email
added_field.source: public/javascripts/review.js's $('#add') click handler sets data.email = userSelected.mail (the Bloodhound AD cache entry's mail attribute, already resolved client-side, previously never sent)

changed_request_body.behavior_change: When uid has no local User record: previously always refused with a 400 telling an admin the person must log in first. Now: ensureUserExists creates the record from {uid, name, email} if email was sent (add proceeds to the existing, unchanged permission check); if email was not sent (older client) or the directory entry had none, the add is refused with the same validation-error shape as any other missing-required-field case, which is no worse than today's outright refusal for that one case.
